title: Many-body quantum optics in a cascaded chiral network
authors: Frank Yang, Parth S. Shah, Chaitali Joshi, Mohammad Mirhosseini
abstract: Chiral quantum emitters interact with light only in one propagation direction, allowing them to be linked into cascaded systems in which photons mediate ordered, long-range interactions. Such systems are predicted to host novel regimes of many-body physics of light and matter. Exploring these regimes requires arrays of identical quantum emitters with directional, low-loss coupling to guided photons, a combination that has thus far remained experimentally out of reach. Here we realize a cascaded network of superconducting qubits using an architecture that overcomes these bottlenecks. We implement a four-qubit chain spanning two modules, with separations ranging from millimeters to half a meter, and exploit the shared waveguide as a dissipative resource to stabilize reconfigurable entanglement, reaching a genuinely multipartite regime unavailable in reciprocal baths. By scattering weak pulses off the chain, we observe photons sorted in time by photon number, a signature of the strong photon-photon interactions mediated by the emitters. Together, these results provide experimental access to many-body light-matter regimes that are beyond the reach of reciprocal systems.
summary: The research reports the experimental creation and characterization of a cascaded network of superconducting qubits designed to mimic chiral quantum emitters. By engineering directional coupling, the system accesses novel many-body physics regimes in light-matter interaction. This work is significant because it demonstrates entanglement and photon correlation signatures unattainable in standard, reciprocal quantum optical setups.
main_problem: The core challenge is realizing and experimentally accessing many-body quantum light-matter interaction regimes mediated by photons in a highly directional, or chiral, manner.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a cascaded superconducting qubit network exhibiting genuine multipartite entanglement and observing photon number sorting, confirming access to physics beyond reciprocal systems.
method: The work combines theoretical modeling using master equations (Liouvillians) with experimental characterization of transmission coefficients and entanglement witnesses on the physical chip.
model_or_system: The system is a cascaded chain of superconducting qubits coupled to a shared microwave waveguide, engineered to exhibit chirality by breaking time-reversal symmetry. The dynamics are modeled using master equations incorporating forward/backward decay channels.
key_observables: Complex transmission phase accumulation ($2\pi N$), genuine multipartite negativity (GMN), and temporal sorting of output photons based on photon number.
important_parameters: The system operates in a regime characterized by strong, directional coupling ($\eta_d \sim 100$) and is sensitive to the relative phases imparted by parametric drives.
main_assumptions: Theoretical analysis often assumes perfect chirality (zero backward decay) or relies on low-power approximations using ABCD matrices for tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the four-qubit chain architecture, measured complex transmission showing phase accumulation with qubit number, and output light sorted in time according to photon number.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform (superconducting qubits) and demonstrating directional coupling signatures, to theoretically modeling the full quantum dynamics via master equations, and finally confirming advanced phenomena like entanglement stabilization and photon-photon interaction signatures.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental realization of chiral cavity QED systems, which are crucial testbeds for understanding non-reciprocal light-matter interactions that cannot be simulated by standard reciprocal waveguide models.
